lesson: PR body must NOT contain any agent self-attribution block (see global rule). Start with the ticket key, scope summary, what changed (file + before/after), how it was validated (Snowflake counts, dbt test name), and acceptance criteria check.

Hard rule: do NOT push or open the PR in any auth mode except FULL_AUTO without an explicit approval pause. Compute the PR shape (title, body, reviewers from CODEOWNERS + recent-PR pattern, labels) deterministically and return it in payload so the operator can review BEFORE approving. Base branch: qa (not main) for finance ARR work. PR title format: `<ticket-key>: <one-line summary>` - no agent self-attribution anywhere.

Refactor-era PR title format: `<EDAEM-XXXX>: <verb> <short scope>` (e.g. `EDAEM-3458: Fix up_for_renewal dual term_end fan-out`). PR body MUST start with the Jira link, scope summary, and any cross-linked Jiras (EDADEV-* for GTM dependencies, semantic-layer PR# for downstream metric changes). Never open a refactor PR without at least one linked Jira.
evidence: Refactored QA / UAT Testing - user explicitly required Jira# in PR name AND link in description.

lesson: Every PROD promotion PR description must include a gate sentence in BOLD at the top: '**DO NOT MERGE until QA PR #N has been validated against <specific number>**'. The number is the metric tie-out value (e.g. '$8.272B BoP ARR T4Q' or '$524M FY26-Q4 incremental'). This forces qa validation BEFORE prod merge — pattern used in #441, #443, #444 with explicit Tableau / Snowflake numbers.

PROD promotion PRs should ALSO include a validation table showing BoP / EoP / Incremental tie-out across affected fiscal quarters, run against `certified_prod` with the new code, so reviewers can see the expected impact BEFORE merge. Example template from #441 / #444: a 5-row T4Q-ending table with BoP, EoP, Incremental, NRR%, GRR% columns.

lesson:
EDAEM PR titles follow predictable prefixes:   'EDAEM-NNNN: <verb> <thing>' — Jira-linked feature/fix
  'fix(<scope>): <thing>' — small focused fix (e.g. fix(fla))
  'feat(<scope>): <thing>' — additive feature
  'perf(<scope>): <thing>' — performance only
  'PROD promotion: <topic> [#qaPR1, #qaPR2]' — prod cherry-pick
  'PROD: <topic> (depends on QA #N)' — alt prod-promotion form
  'chore: <thing>' — infra / tooling / docs
  'Revert <thing> (PRs #X, #Y)' / 'Roll back #X' — revert
  'Append N <thing> rows for FY<X>-Q<Y> (<accts>)' — seed append
Pick the matching prefix for new PRs so qa/prod history stays greppable by intent.

lesson: Empty / template-only PR bodies are technical debt. Real examples in window: #450 (REVERTED — body was empty template), #461 (body was literally 'Test QA CD job' for a CD validation that re-enabled a CX dependency — buried the intent). When the PR body is empty, future-you must reconstruct intent from the diff + Slack + Jira. Minimum body for any PR: (1) Jira link or explicit no-ticket reason, (2) business motivation in 1-2 lines, (3) the data change (what columns/grains move), (4) the code change (which files), (5) validation plan with concrete tie-out values where applicable.
